excerpt: Pin a policy page and every agent that can read it sees it each turn.
Edit it, and running agents get the new version on their next turn.
Each customer's or team's pages live in their own scope, and the scopes your server passes for a run decide which ones it can read.
People and agents can add notes without rewriting the page.
Pages nest like folders, so `org:acme#policies/refund` is the `refund` page under `policies` in the `org:acme` scope.
These links make Knowledge a graph rather than a list of documents.
A research agent writes findings, a planning agent adds a plan under them, and a coding agent reads both from the same scope.
Load your docs or policies into a scope and give the agent read-only tools.
Search only returns pages the run can read, so a run that holds a different `org:` scope doesn't find Acme's page.
a viewer reads, a contributor adds pages and notes, an editor changes pages, and an owner can also delete pages and move them between scopes.
Memory is optional: an agent without it works too, as long as each call passes `scopes`, but [pinned context](/docs/knowledge/pinned-context) needs Memory.
To see the page, run `mastra dev`, open Studio and select **Knowledge**.
`KNOWLEDGE_ROUTES` turns on the Knowledge page in Studio, which shows every scope and page as a tree beside a graph of how the pages link.
With Knowledge, an agent can not only read information but update it too, allowing it to learn and self-improve over time.
`knowledge_list` lists the pages in a scope.
Knowledge is stored in your configured storage provider, which adds its own `mastra_knowledge_*` tables the first time Knowledge is used
For updates, the agent writes the page to the scope that matches the request.
You can run separate knowledge bases per function, like coding and support, and set permissions at the individual, team and org level.
You connect the systems where your org already writes, like Slack and Monday, and Knowledge keeps itself current.
